# Triage one issue

You are triaging one GitHub issue in this repo, unattended, from the Triage workflow. The issue number is in your task. Use `gh` for every issue operation; it is already signed in as the repo owner.

## Read first

1. The issue: `gh issue view <n> --json number,title,body,labels,comments`.
2. `docs/agents/triage-labels.md` and `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.
3. `CLAUDE.md`, `GLOSSARY.md` and every record in `docs/out-of-scope/`.
4. The code the issue touches, enough to judge its size and risk. For a bug, try to reproduce it (with `bun run test`, or a small test of your own you then discard), or find the cause in the code.
5. Open issues, for duplicates: `gh issue list --state open --json number,title,labels`.

Don't change any code, commit or push. You only edit the issue.

## Decide

Pick exactly one category label from the Categories table in `docs/agents/triage-labels.md`: `bug`, `enhancement` or `documentation`.

Pick exactly one outcome:

- **`ready`**: the issue meets every point of [the `ready` bar](../../docs/agents/triage-labels.md#the-ready-bar). It then waits in Ready for an agent to build it with no one watching, so apply it only when you are sure. When in doubt, it isn't `ready`.
- **`needs-info`**: you have questions only the owner can answer.
- **`ready-for-human`**: it's clear, but fails the `ready` bar. If it touches the [hand-back list](../../docs/agents/issue-tracker.md#hand-back-list), say which item.
- **`wontfix`**: a duplicate, already done, covered by an out-of-scope record, or not worth doing. Apply the label and recommend it in your comment; never close the issue: the owner does.

## Write

Start every comment and every issue body you write with this line, then a blank line:

```
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*
```

1. **For `ready` only**, promote a short spec into the issue body (see "Promote, don't duplicate" in `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`). First post the original body as a comment that starts with the disclaimer, then `Original note:`, then the original body. Then write the new body to a file and `gh issue edit <n> --body-file <file>`. The spec has: a one-line summary, current and desired behaviour, acceptance criteria as a `- [ ]` checklist (each checkable by a test or a screenshot), and what is out of scope. Use the glossary's terms. Retitle the issue if the scope changed.
2. **Comment** with your reasons: which outcome, and why, point by point against the `ready` bar. For `needs-info`, list your questions as a numbered list. For `wontfix`, name the duplicate issue or the out-of-scope record.
3. **Labels**, last, in one command, so nothing sees `ready` before the spec is written: add the category and the outcome, and remove `needs-triage` and any other category or outcome label already on the issue. For example `gh issue edit <n> --add-label bug,ready --remove-label needs-triage`.

Don't set the board Status: the workflow does it from the labels.
